page: Vultr voc-g-40c-160gb-768s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring 40 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, utilizing 20 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core. The system is equipped with 160.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 768 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core capabilities and high memory bandwidth. The server achieves top-tier status in uncached large-block memory bandwidth, with read speeds of 451.84 GB/sec and write speeds of 262.45 GB/sec. Multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng and Geekbench is strong, placing in the top 25% of tested hardware. Cryptographic and vector operations are supported by hardware-accelerated AES, SHA_NI, and AVX instructions, resulting in strong Passmark CPU encryption and extended instruction scores. Single-core performance, static web serving, and text processing fall within the average tier.

From a resource density perspective, this instance offers high qualitative cost efficiency for multi-threaded workloads due to its dedicated AMD EPYC cores and high memory bandwidth. However, single-threaded tasks do not benefit from the same relative performance advantage, as shown by average single-core Geekbench and compression scores. The absence of AVX-512 and AMX instructions represents a tradeoff for specialized deep learning workloads, though the server still delivers strong text generation speeds on medium-sized 7B LLM models.

This server is well-suited for multi-threaded applications, database operations, and memory-intensive processing. Appropriate workloads include Redis deployments, software compilation, ray tracing, and medium-scale LLM text generation.
